days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Kvitneset
stops.detail: The fjord opens between the peninsulas of Kvitneset in Hareidlandet and Eltraneset on the island of Sula.

stops.name: Sjøholt
stops.detail: South of the island of Sula, the Storfjord turns inland, heading east until Sjøholt, then south.

stops.name: Hellesylt
stops.detail: The latter extends southwards as far as Hellesylt.

stops.name: Adlerstraße
stops.detail: Along the inner part of the fjord, the Sunnylvsfjord and the Geirangerfjord, there are no roads at all except at Hellesylt, where Fylkesvei 60 follows the fjord again for a few kilometers, and at Geiranger, where Fv63 comes over a pass from Eidsdal as the Eagle Road and then drops down to the fjord and follows it to Geiranger.

stops.name: Hjørundfjord
stops.detail: The largest side branch of the Storfjord is the Hjørundfjord.

stops.name: Norangstfjord
stops.detail: It extends in a south-southeasterly direction and branches after 22 km into the smaller branch Norangstfjord and the larger branch Storfjord, which is identified by the municipality name Ørsta to distinguish it from the main fjord of the same name, even though the namesake central town of this municipality lies on a western side branch of the Vartdalsfjord.
